blocks.text: Admins manage who has access to the Omnisient Platform. From here you can invite new users, edit their details and permissions, and deactivate users who no longer need access.
Permissions: Only users with Admin permissions can access Users.
In the Omnisient Platform, go to Admin > Users. The Users page lists all the users in your company.
Adding a user to the Omnisient Platform
The new user receives a welcome email with:

items: A link to set a secure password
A link to download and install Desktop Connect
Their login email and instructions for logging in to the Platform and Desktop Connect
A link to the Help Center for further guidance
Open the actions menu next to the user and select Edit.
Open the actions menu next to the user and select Deactivate.
Confirm in the dialog that appears.

blocks.text: Deactivation can't be undone, so if you're deactivating your own account as an Admin, make sure another Admin is available first. Doing so immediately removes your access to the Platform and Desktop Connect.

items: Open the actions menu next to the user and select Edit Permissions.

blocks.text: As different companies may have varying roles and responsibilities, users with Admin privileges can configure permissions according to their specific requirements. Admin users can modify the profiles of user-type users, restricting their access to only the functions that are relevant to their responsibilities.

By granting different levels of access and allowing Admin users to customize permissions, the Omnisient Platform ensures that each user has tailored access to the necessary features and functionalities based on their role within the company.
Role: Each user is either a User or an Admin. Refer to the tables below for permissions.

rows: Make Selections, Downloads, Delete and Reload Selections

title: Assigning User Permissions During Project Creation

blocks.text: User access is configured during the first step of the project creation wizard. You can add users from your organization and assign their roles before the project is submitted.

Quick summary: Add users and assign roles in the first step of project creation. Search and select users by name or email. Default permission is Read Only, with easy dropdown editing. Reduce access errors and streamline collaboration from day one.

This feature is ideal for all users creating new projects on the Omnisient platform, especially those managing teams or projects that require input from multiple collaborators within the same organization.
Begin by clicking Create New Project and selecting your project template.
In the first step of the wizard, you'll now see a section labeled “User Access and Permissions”.

items: Use the search bar to find users by name or email address.
Only users from your organization are shown.
Users already added to the project won't appear again in the search.

blocks.text: 3. View and manage the user list
Once selected, users appear under the “Users” section with their name and email.

items: You, the project creator, will automatically be listed as Owner.
Your role and the delete option will be disabled (since you can't remove yourself).
All added users are given Read Only permission by default.

blocks.text: Next to each user's name, a dropdown allows you to assign their role: Owner, Read and Write, or Read Only.

rows: Full control: can manage users, edit all content, delete the project, and update permissions.
Can view and edit the project, manage data and reports, and perform selections.
View-only access to the project, data, and reports, with no editing capabilities.

blocks.text: To remove a user before completing project setup, simply click the delete icon.

items: Set permissions based on responsibilities: Only assign Owner permissions to those who truly need full control.
Keep access lean: Avoid over-permissioning, more is not always better.
Review before publishing: Take a moment to confirm all necessary users and roles are in place.

blocks.text: Activity Log is an audit trail that records account activity across the Omnisient Platform: what happened, who did it, and when. It gives Admin users visibility into user actions and permission changes without needing to check with the team.
Permissions: Only users with Admin permissions can access Activity Log. See the User Management chapter.
In the Omnisient Platform, go to Admin > Activity Log.
Every entry in the Activity Log includes four fields:

rows: The specific detail of that action
The email address of the user who performed it
Narrow the log to the last 1, 2, or 3 months.
Export to CSV. The export includes all four fields (Action, Activity, User, Date) for the selected date range.

blocks.text: Approvals is where you control what partners can do with your shared data. When a partner creates a project or a SQLPad export using your dataset, the request goes to Approvals, where an Admin decides whether it's allowed to proceed.
Permissions: Only users with Admin permissions can access Approvals. See the User Management chapter.
In the Omnisient Platform, go to Admin > Approvals. This is your central hub for reviewing every request.
You'll get an email notification when a new request comes in, with a direct link to review it.
Make sure to action requests promptly. If a request isn't actioned in time, it will lock and the partner will be blocked.
blocks.bold_lead: Make sure to action requests promptly.

blocks.text: Approving projects created on your data gives you control, visibility, and peace of mind around how your data is being used. This process is designed to be simple and transparent, so you always stay in the loop.

rows: The dataset share behind the request has expired, or the subscription has expired.

items: Find the request and click Review in the final column.
Check the request details in the modal that opens. The review shows the request details, along with the shared dataset that the partner wants to use to create the project.

rows: The requestor gets a confirmation email and the request moves into processing.
A modal opens asking for a rejection reason. Be specific here. It appears in the requestor's rejection email, so a clear reason means they know exactly what to fix before resubmitting their request.

blocks.text: The review modal breaks the request into two sections:

rows: The name of the partner, the project type, date of request and project code.
The shared dataset's name, dates, status, and who shared it.

blocks.text: Approving SQLPad exports is an important part of ensuring that your data is used responsibly and transparently. It gives you clear visibility into how your data contributes to insights, while keeping you in control of what gets exported.
Once a SQLPad export is approved, Omnisient can no longer track or control copies saved locally by the user.

items: Find the request and click Review in the final column.
Check the request details in the modal that opens.

rows: This will now be followed by an additional security check by Omnisient.
A modal opens asking for a rejection reason. Be specific here. It appears in the requestor's rejection email, so a clear reason means they know exactly what to fix before resubmitting their request.

blocks.text: The review modal breaks the request into six sections:

rows: Overview of what the export contains.

blocks.text: If your firewall is blocking the installation or use of the Omnisient app, send the URLs below to your IT administrator to add to your allowlist.
You only need the domains for the region your organization uses, plus the General Domains, which apply to everyone.

The IP ranges (Cloudflare + Azure) are only needed for firewalls that filter by IP rather than domain/hostname. Since Omnisient sits behind Cloudflare and Azure's shared infrastructure rather than having dedicated static IPs, IP-based firewalls require the full published ranges rather than a single specific address.
Omnisient is served through Cloudflare. If your firewall filters by IP address, your IT team should also allow Cloudflare's IP ranges, published at https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/
